overview.body: This is a MASTER unit, and the last lab of the semester. Look at what your game keeps track of during one trip: current_city, total_miles, total_turns, total_hazards, total_escaped, visited_cities, hazards_list, unique_cities, unique_hazards, trivia_asked, and trivia_correct. Eleven variables, all describing one player's trip. This lab you bundle them into a Player class, with a getter and a setter for every one. The provided lab-5-2.py is your Lab 5.1 game with those variables replaced by one Player object. It won't run until you write player.py, and when it does, it prints exactly what your Lab 5.1 printed.

mentorQuote.quote: Last week the cities became objects. This week the player does. Same game, same trivia, same beach, and the code finally reads like the story: a player travels to a city, faces a hazard, answers a question.

content.code:
class Player:
    """
    One player's trip in the road trip game.

    Private attributes:
        __name (str): The player's name
        __current_city (str): Where the player is now
        __total_miles (int): Miles traveled this game
        __total_turns (int): Turns taken this game
        __total_hazards (int): Hazards faced this game
        __total_escaped (int): Hazards escaped this game
        __visited_cities (list): Every stop, in order
        __hazards_list (list): Every hazard faced, in order
        __unique_cities (set): Each city visited, once
        __unique_hazards (set): Each hazard faced, once
        __trivia_asked (int): Trivia questions asked this game
        __trivia_correct (int): Trivia questions answered right
    """

    def __init__(self, name):
        """
        Start a new trip in San Antonio.

        Args:
            name (str): The player's name
        """
        self.__name = name
        self.__current_city = 'San Antonio'
        self.__total_miles = 0
        self.__total_turns = 0
        self.__total_hazards = 0
        self.__total_escaped = 0
        self.__visited_cities = ['San Antonio']
        self.__hazards_list = []
        self.__unique_cities = set(self.__visited_cities)
        self.__unique_hazards = set(self.__hazards_list)
        self.__trivia_asked = 0
        self.__trivia_correct = 0

    def __str__(self):
        """Return the player as text, like 'Tester in Houston (200 miles)'."""
        return (f'{self.__name} in {self.__current_city} '
                f'({self.__total_miles} miles)')

In Lab 5.1, arriving in a city took five lines spread through the travel loop: the miles, the turns, the current city, the route list, and the unique-city set. Miss one and the trip report is wrong. content.code:
def travel_to(self, city, miles, turns):
        """
        Record arriving in a city.

        Args:
            city (str): The city the player arrived in
            miles (int): Miles traveled to get there
            turns (int): Turns it took to get there
        """
        self.__current_city = city
        self.__total_miles = self.__total_miles + miles
        self.__total_turns = self.__total_turns + turns
        self.__visited_cities.append(city)
        self.__unique_cities.add(city)

    def record_hazard(self, name, escaped):
        """
        Record one hazard.

        Args:
            name (str): The hazard's name
            escaped (bool): True if the player escaped it
        """
        self.__total_hazards = self.__total_hazards + 1
        if escaped:
            self.__total_escaped = self.__total_escaped + 1
        self.__hazards_list.append(name)
        self.__unique_hazards.add(name)

    def record_trivia(self, correct):
        """
        Record one trivia question.

        Args:
            correct (bool): True if the player answered right
        """
        self.__trivia_asked = self.__trivia_asked + 1
        if correct:
            self.__trivia_correct = self.__trivia_correct + 1

checkpoints.title: Pick Up Where You Left Off

content.body: One more method, resume(), so a loaded game can hand its saved trip to a new Player. That finishes the class: every path through the game works, saving and loading included.

Every game starts with a new Player in San Antonio. When the player loads a save, the game still makes a new Player, then calls player.resume(...) with the seven trip values from the save file. Trivia counts aren't saved, so they stay at zero, the same as Lab 4.3.

content.quote: You wrote the same game five different ways this semester, and each time it got better. Module 1 was raw Python. Module 2 added loops and functions. Module 3 added files. Module 4 added dictionaries. Module 5 brings it home with objects. Every rewrite taught you something the last one couldn't, and that's how you learn to build things that last.

items: Below record_trivia(), add resume(). Its first line is long, so it breaks after total_turns, with the rest lined up under self. It sets the seven attributes, then rebuilds both sets from the new lists:

content.code:
def resume(self, current_city, total_miles, total_turns,
               total_hazards, total_escaped, visited_cities, hazards_list):
        """
        Pick up a saved trip where it left off. Trivia counts aren't
        saved, so they stay at zero.

        Args:
            current_city (str): Where the saved trip stopped
            total_miles (int): Miles traveled so far
            total_turns (int): Turns taken so far
            total_hazards (int): Hazards faced so far
            total_escaped (int): Hazards escaped so far
            visited_cities (list): Every stop so far, in order
            hazards_list (list): Every hazard so far, in order
        """
        self.__current_city = current_city
        self.__total_miles = total_miles
        self.__total_turns = total_turns
        self.__total_hazards = total_hazards
        self.__total_escaped = total_escaped
        self.__visited_cities = visited_cities
        self.__hazards_list = hazards_list
        self.__unique_cities = set(visited_cities)
        self.__unique_hazards = set(hazards_list)
